newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsui Petrochem, Mitsui Toatsu to merge--paper.
newsitem.headline: Mitsui Petrochem, Mitsui Toatsu to merge--paper.

text.p: Mitsui Petrochemical Industries Ltd and Mitsui Toatsu Chemicals Inc have agreed to merge in October 1997 to become the second-largest petrochemical company in Japan, a Japanese newspaper said on Monday.
Both Mitsui Petrochemical and Mitsui Toatsu spokesmen declined to comment on the report.
Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said Mitsui Toatsu would be dissolved on the merger. It said 0.5 to 0.6 Mitsui Petrochemical shares would be exchanged for one Mitsui Toatsu share.
The merger was decided to increase the two companies' international competitiveness, the paper said.
Parent sales of the new company, expected to be called Mitsui Chemical, would be about 700 billion yen in the year to March 31, 1997, the paper said.
The new company would produce materials for plastics, fertilisers, pharmaceutical products, electronics products and other petrochemical products, the paper said.
